name: flood-risk-analysis-action-stage-lead
instruction:
Measure how much advance notice action-stage water levels provided before flooding during July 1–8, 2025. The two inputs in `/root/work` are `gage_height_iv.rdb` and `nws_gauges.csv`. The RDB file contains tab-separated USGS-style instantaneous readings: discard lines beginning `#`, read the next line as column names, and skip the following field-type line. Its `datetime` field is local time, `site_no` is a text station ID, and `00065` is gage height in feet. Blank heights are missing. The NWS-style CSV has columns `usgs id`, `action stage`, and `flood stage`, all thresholds in feet; each data row also has one unnamed trailing field that must be ignored. Preserve leading zeroes in station IDs.

For each station and calendar date, use the maximum available gage height. Identify its first date at or above action stage and its first date at or above flood stage during the stated period. Report only stations that reached flood stage. The action date may equal the flood date; lead time is the difference between those calendar dates in whole days, not elapsed hours between readings. Stations with no usable height on a date have no threshold crossing on that date.

Write `/root/work/action_lead_times.tsv` as tab-separated text with a header and exactly these columns: `station_id`, `first_action_date`, `first_flood_date`, `lead_days`. Use `YYYY-MM-DD` dates and integer lead days. Sort rows by station ID ascending; include no summary or comment lines.
